transcription.notes: Not a photograph: transcribed from the text of the official Strat-O-Matic Baseball 365 example pitcher card (Don Drysdale 1965) published on Strat-O-Matic's own help page https://365.strat-o-matic.com/help/pitchercard (retrieved 2026-11-03). The card is HTML text, so every cell is exact. Read twice independently: (1) parsed from the HTML table structure, (2) re-split from the tag-stripped text by roll prefixes; 0 differences across 66 cells. 'raw' keeps the 365 rendering verbatim, roll prefix and glyph included. 365 prints flyball X-chances as 'FB(cf)X'; outcomes spell them 'FLY (cf) X', the corpus spelling the importer reads, and raw keeps 'FB'. The 365 glyphs are recorded in 'markers' under the meanings in the page's legend: '#' = ballparkHR, '>' = ballparkSingle, and '@' = atSign. The legend says 365 ignores '@' because it uses pitch-count fatigue instead; it is probably the board game's fatigue mark, but that is unconfirmed. Outcomes hold the printed result, which is what the importer reads. The 365 card is Strat-O-Matic's own digital rendering of its 1965 season advanced card. It is official product data, but not a photographed physical card.
